conviction_note: Evidence on demand is good: optical peers that reported after Semtech last spoke beat and raised, Coherent by +17% q/q datacenter and MACOM by +37% q/q datacenter. But the reported quarter was pre-raised on 2026-10-15, and in this tape a direct peer's beat-and-raise was sold 18% while SMTC fell 17.5% the same day. The stock also ran +18% intraday today into the print, against a +16.7pt put skew. So the per-finding sum is slightly negative (-0.6) while the scaled lean is a near-coin-flip slightly up (p_up 52 x abs 13 = +0.52). The two disagree in sign because the sum carries the sector's sell-the-beat reaction and today's run-up as explicit negatives, while p_up leans on the name's own record (beat-and-raise prints bought +10.4%, +15.1%, +21.1%) and on peer data that supports a strong January-quarter guide.

findings.finding: The reported quarter was pre-announced. On 2026-10-15, about ten days before the quarter ended, Semtech raised Q3 FY27 to $415-420M revenue and $1.12-1.16 EPS (from $410M +/-5M and $1.05 +/-0.03). Consensus of $416M/$1.13 (Zacks) to $424M/$1.15 (Chartmill) sits inside or at the top of that range. A print of about $420-425M is a beat of roughly 1-2% on a bar the company itself set.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide raise itself on 2026-10-15 was sold: an intraday low of $133.66 against a $153.20 open, attributed to an underwhelming FY2030 $3.2B framework. In Aug 2026, a beat of $341.9M against a $328M guide plus a $410M guide bought +10.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced. The quarter was raised publicly 10 days before it ended, so only the distance above $420M is new. If the market expected a large Q3 upside, the stock would not sit 48% off its high with a +16.7pt put skew.
findings.independence: Same raise also reported in https://finviz.com/news/403570/semtech-shares-rise-27-as-higher-q3-guidance-and-northland-upgrade-support-recovery (2026-10-16). EDGAR shows the 8-K item 7.01 filed 2026-10-15. All three describe one document.

findings.finding: MACOM, a direct peer in optical TIAs, drivers and LPO analog, reported on 2026-11-05, three weeks after Semtech last spoke. Datacenter revenue was a record $188.1M (+37% q/q), it guided datacenter +15% q/q for the Dec quarter, book-to-bill was 1.4, and backlog was a record. This shows optical analog demand was still accelerating through Oct-Dec, which supports Semtech's Q4 (Jan quarter) datacenter guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SMTC's guide-driven prints: Aug 2026 +10.41%, Aug 2025 +15.14%, Mar 2025 +21.06% when guides were strong; Mar 2026 -11.0%. But the peer's own strong guide was sold 18.35% (see the positioning finding).
findings.why_not_priced: Semtech's Q4 guide consensus was set before the MACOM print, and SMTC fell 17.5% on the day MACOM reported instead of rising. If this read-through were in the price, SMTC would not have de-rated in step with the peer's selloff. Net of the rest of the company: datacenter is about 35-40% of Semtech's Q3 revenue (guided about $145M+ of ~$417M). LoRa (record $58M) and IoT/AMS need only hold flat for the datacenter read-through to carry the total.
findings.independence: Coherent (separate document, next finding) points the same way: https://finviz.com/news/415844/coherent-corp-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-results

findings.finding: Coherent reported its Sep quarter on 2026-11-04. Datacenter revenue rose +17% q/q and +85% y/y, 1.6T transceivers are ramping with multiple customers and are expected to 'ramp rapidly over the coming quarters', and the Dec-quarter guide is $2.55-2.75B (about +12% q/q). Semtech targets more than 50% share of 1.6T FiberEdge by fiscal year-end, so the module-maker ramp feeds its Jan-quarter guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SMTC rose on the Aug 2026 print, when 1.6T FiberEdge ramp commentary drove +10.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: The customer-side 1.6T acceleration landed after Semtech's last guide update (10-15), and SMTC fell 22% from 10-28 to 11-13 regardless. If the market were pricing a stronger 1.6T ramp into Semtech's Jan quarter, the stock would not be at about 20x a Q3 EPS run-rate. This is a proxy, not Semtech's own number: Coherent builds some of its own drivers/TIAs, so the transmission is not one-for-one.
findings.independence: MACOM finding above (different company, different document). Innolight also said 800G and 1.6T orders rose q/q: https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3372672/chinas-optical-suppliers-extend-sell-fears-slower-ai-growth-trump-upbeat-earnings

findings.finding: The Chinese module makers that buy Semtech's 1.6T components were mixed for the Sep quarter. Innolight revenue was +172% y/y with 800G/1.6T orders up q/q, but 3% below consensus. Eoptolink revenue fell 13% q/q on shortages of key components and a delayed 1.6T capacity ramp. Inventories rose 20% (Innolight) and 49% (Eoptolink) q/q. A stretched component supply chain and swelling module-maker inventory raise a digestion question for component suppliers' next guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct SMTC history on this line. The Chinese optical names sold off on the results day (SCMP).
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: these results came out 10-30, before SMTC's November slide, so they are part of why the sector de-rated. Inventory build can equally mean Semtech's chips were pulled in, which supports its Q3/Q4 sell-in. The article does not say which components were short, so the sign is uncertain and the size small.
findings.independence: SCMP on the same prints: https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3372672/chinas-optical-suppliers-extend-sell-fears-slower-ai-growth-trump-upbeat-earnings. Same underlying results, so one finding.

findings.finding: NVIDIA reported its October quarter on 2026-11-19: revenue of $115.8B (+20% q/q, +103% y/y) against about $109.0B expected, and a Jan-quarter guide of $130B +/-3% (about +12% q/q). The AI buildout that drives Semtech's datacenter line kept accelerating into the Jan quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for SMTC on NVIDIA prints specifically. SMTC kept falling into 11-20 ($87.63 close) after NVIDIA's beat, then rose 18% today.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: today's +18% may be the delayed response. This is macro-to-company transmission, not a Semtech number, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy. Coherent and MACOM datacenter guides (above) are the direct counterparties.

findings.finding: Reaction function in this tape: MACOM beat ($424.8M vs $420.2M; EPS $2.09 vs $2.00) and guided up (Dec quarter $450-460M, datacenter +15% q/q, book-to-bill 1.4), and its stock fell 18.35% after earnings; SMTC fell 17.5% on 2026-11-05 alongside. Semtech's own raised Q3 guide and FY2030 framework on 10-15 were also sold, to an intraday low of $133.66 from a $153.20 open. Optical analog beat-and-raise prints have recently been sold on capex-cadence fears.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SMTC's own beat-and-raise prints were bought (Aug 2026 +10.41%, Aug 2025 +15.14%), but the two most recent good-news events in this sector (SMTC Analyst Day 10-15, MACOM 11-05) were sold hard.
findings.why_not_priced: The put skew (+16.7) prices this risk in part. What is not visible in SMTC's own reaction history (4 of 7 up, good guides bought) is that the sector's reaction function flipped in October-November. SMTC has since fallen another ~20%, so the bar for 'good enough' may have dropped, which is why this is sized below the peer's -18%.
findings.independence: Same-day SMTC move: https://www.trefis.com/stock/smtc/articles/625295/should-you-buy-the-dip-in-semtech-stock-now/2026-11-16 (17.5% drop on 11-05). Analyst Day selloff: https://finviz.com/news/403570/semtech-shares-rise-27-as-higher-q3-guidance-and-northland-upgrade-support-recovery

findings.finding: SMTC ran up about 18% intraday today into the print, from an $87.63 prior close to ~$103.3-103.5, on a broad tech rally and early-session volume about 79% below average. Part of the relief a solid print would bring is already in the sealed spot of $103.41.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior SMTC print came after an 18% same-day run-up. The 5-day run-up is still -1.79% and the 20-day -24.4%, so the stock is not stretched on longer windows.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The question is whether the sealed entry already holds the print's upside. A same-day +18% on thin volume with no company news (Webull cites a minor TDS2621LP product launch) is short covering or beta, and can unwind on anything short of a decisive guide.

findings.finding: The cellular module business is held for sale to Compal for $62M and is expected to close in fiscal Q4 (the Jan quarter). In Q2 it contributed $48.1M of revenue at about 23% adjusted gross margin, and the company says the sale is neutral to non-GAAP EPS. If the deal closes inside Q4, the headline Q4 revenue guide loses up to ~$48M a quarter, so it could print flat-to-down q/q against $417.5M even with datacenter growing. A headline-reading reaction or a consensus that still includes cellular could misread the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Semtech print with a divestiture-truncated guide.
findings.why_not_priced: No sourced Q4 consensus is visible, so it cannot be shown whether consensus excludes cellular. Margins will optically rise (63.9% ex-cellular GM guide vs 58.3%), which offsets. Sophisticated holders will model it, so this is small.
findings.independence: Q2 release figures for the held-for-sale business: https://www.semtech.com/company/press/semtech-announces-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027-results

findings.finding: On the Aug call management said the rest of FY27 was fully booked and FY28 more than 70% booked, but existing capacity may not cover FY28 demand, especially in the second half. Semtech is buying equipment, making prepayments and adding manufacturing partners. Q4 and the FY28 commentary are therefore supply-gated rather than demand-gated, which supports a firm guide and caps upside at capacity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 print carrying this booking commentary bought +10.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since August. What is new on the call is whether capacity was secured (upside to FY28) or remains the binding constraint (a capped guide). The stock's 48% de-rating says the market doubts the duration of demand, not the booked FY27.
findings.independence: The same booking/backlog language is in the Q2 release ('record backlog', 'visibility expected to extend well into next fiscal year'): https://www.semtech.com/company/press/semtech-announces-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027-results

findings.finding: Balance sheet at Q2: $143.4M of debt became current (up from zero at FY-end; convertible notes coming due), long-term debt was $349.4M, cash $204.1M, and the period carried 'induced conversion expense'. Debt refinancing or convert settlement could come with the print. What the money buys: capacity prepayments for a booked ramp (Q2 FCF $61.4M), so this is not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for SMTC on a financing line at a print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is visible in the Q2 balance sheet. FCF of $61.4M a quarter and $204M of cash cover the current portion, and the money funds a booked ramp, so the sign is zero.
findings.independence: Same document as the capacity finding (Q2 release). Counted once here, on the financing line.

findings.finding: SMTC's November de-rating has dated sector/macro causes, not company news. On 11-04 SMTC fell 13% on fears of a Texas data-center construction pause and the possible end of tax incentives after the midterms (Texas is about 27% of planned US data-center GW, per Wells Fargo). On 11-16 chips sold off on Fed hike odds rising to about 85%. The stock is now about $103 against FY2030 targets of $12.40-13 adj. EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SMTC fell 13% on 11-04 and traded down on 11-16 with the group.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: these causes are the drawdown itself. Filed so the judges see the drawdown has a macro cause that the print cannot resolve, unless management addresses customer capex or Texas exposure on the call. Sized 0.

outside_window.finding: Cellular module sale to Compal ($62M) closing, expected in fiscal Q4 FY27 (Nov 2026-Jan 2027), subject to regulatory approvals. A closing announcement after 11-24 would not reach this window.
Credo and Marvell, both datacenter connectivity peers, report in early December, after this window. Their read-across cannot reach this trade.

baseline_tension: The fundamental read (peer datacenter beats and raises after Semtech's last update; NVIDIA accelerating) cuts against the +16.7pt put skew and the -24% 20-day run-up. Today's +18% intraday jump and the sector's habit of selling beat-and-raise prints this autumn side with the skew, so the scaled lean is held near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guided range): the Q3 reported-quarter finding lands inside the 10-15 raised guide, so it was cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the MACOM and Coherent datacenter read-throughs rest on ~35-40% of revenue, so each was cut from +1.0 to +0.8, net of flat LoRa/IoT/AMS.
Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): a positive lean against a +16.7pt put skew, with short interest at 7.3% of float (not crowded), moved p_up from 54 to 52.
Lesson 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 12 to 13, between the 10.4% median reaction and the 13.5% straddle, with 146% realised vol.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the current debt and capacity prepayments fund a booked ramp, so that finding stays at 0, not negative.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): already carried by the -1.5 sector sell-the-beat positioning finding; not applied a second time to the peer findings.
